security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation or example-code false positives, including Markdown backticks, animation terminology, relative references, and media assets. Real residual risk remains in the optional package bootstrap loader, which can spawn npm, dynamically import dependencies, and fall back to @latest for helper packages.

remediation.issue: Optional helper bootstrap can install dependencies through npm.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer requiring users to install trusted helper packages explicitly, or vendor a fixed helper. Keep --ignore-scripts and confirmation if bootstrap remains.
Reject @latest and require HYPERFRAMES_SKILL_PKG_VERSION or a bundled version before running npm install.

remediation.issue: Dynamic import resolves packages from project and configured node_modules paths.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict package resolution to trusted locations and avoid importing from environment-provided paths unless the user opts in.

remediation.issue: WebGPU guidance enables unsafe browser features for some render workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Document that these flags should be used only with trusted local compositions and never with untrusted remote pages.

content.value_statement: Animation work can drift across timing, runtime, and scene structure. This skill gives HyperFrames rules, blueprints, adapters, and an audit script for deterministic motion.
actual_capabilities: Select atomic motion rules by trigger, tag, or desired animation effect.
Apply multi-phase blueprints for product demos, brand reveals, workflows, and data scenes.
Map runtime choices across GSAP, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, CSS, WAAPI, and TypeGPU.
Use transition guidance for CSS-driven scene changes and paced visual continuity.
Run an animation-map audit script to summarize timelines, tweens, bboxes, collisions, dead zones, and staggers.
Reference named text-animation effects and composition constraints for seek-safe rendering.
limitations: It assumes HyperFrames composition rules from the companion core skill.
It does not create finished media without a separate render pipeline.
The audit script requires Node and may bootstrap helper packages after explicit approval.
Some examples depend on browser animation libraries or GPU features that may vary by environment.

best_practices: Start with two to four atomic rules before loading a full blueprint.
Keep all timelines paused, seek-safe, and registered before rendering begins.
Use the animation-map audit after authoring complex scenes.
anti_patterns: Mixing unbounded repeats or wall-clock timing into render-critical animation.
Using layout-changing properties when transforms can produce the same motion.
Loading every reference file before deciding which scene or runtime is needed.

faq.question: Does this skill replace HyperFrames core guidance?
faq.answer: No. It depends on the core composition contract for duration, seek behavior, and deterministic rendering.

faq.question: Which runtime should I choose first?
faq.answer: Use GSAP first for most motion work. Choose Lottie, Three.js, CSS, WAAPI, Anime.js, or TypeGPU for specific needs.

faq.question: Can it help with existing compositions?
faq.answer: Yes. The animation-map workflow helps review tweens, timing density, dead zones, collisions, and element lifecycles.

faq.question: Does it include runnable examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes example HTML files, assets, blueprints, and runtime-specific recipe documents.

faq.question: Does the audit script need dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses HyperFrames helper packages and can bootstrap them when the user explicitly approves that step.

faq.question: Is it only for text animation?
faq.answer: No. It covers text effects, UI motion, transitions, 3D scenes, data motion, runtime adapters, and choreography audits.
